title: "Data collection"

---

The NCC-study (Koronastudien) combines **self-reported questionnaire data**
with **linked national health-registry data** and **biological samples**. This
page describes each of those sources, how participants consent, and how the
data reaches the secure processing environment. For how the resulting datasets
are structured and joined, see
[Data management](../best-practices/data-management.qmd).

## Overview

Data is collected through three channels that are later linked on a single
participant key:

1. **Questionnaires** — participants answer online questionnaires hosted on
   **Nettskjema**, the University of Oslo's survey platform.
2. **Health registries** — national health registries contribute records for
   consenting participants under the study's approvals.
3. **Biological samples** — biobank and laboratory results (e.g. serology from
   dried blood spots).

All three are delivered into **TSD** (Tjenester for Sensitive Data), where they
are processed into research-ready datasets. Person-level data never leaves TSD.

::: {.callout-tip}
Every source is ultimately keyed to `deltaker_id`, the study's unique
participant identifier, which is what makes the sources joinable. How that key
is assigned is covered under
[Participant identification](#participant-identification).
:::

## Questionnaires

Questionnaires are the core data-collection instrument. Each questionnaire is a
Nettskjema form, and every questionnaire is identified by a single-letter
family used as the prefix on all of its variables.

| Family | Type | Forms | Purpose |
|--------|------|-------|---------|
| **B** | Baseline | B1, B2 | Enrolment questionnaire(s) capturing background at study entry |
| **F** | Follow-up | F1–F6 (F7+ planned) | Repeated follow-up over the course of the study |
| **R** | Report | R1–R6 | CLOC sub-study report questionnaires |
| **E** | Extra | E1, E2, E3 | Supplementary instruments — E2 has sub-forms (BRIEF, RAND-12, ISARIC) |
| **Q** | Quick | Q1 | Short quick-response questionnaire |

### How questionnaire data is collected

- Participants complete questionnaires online in Nettskjema.
- Each submission is a single response; a participant answers a given
  questionnaire at most once, which is why the delivered data is naturally
  **wide** (one row per participant per form).
- Nettskjema assigns each submission an internal reference
  (`submission_reference`). This is used during processing to identify the
  participant, but is **not** stable across re-exports and is not a research
  variable.
- The questionnaire item text and response options are the authoritative
  definition of each variable; they are preserved as variable and value labels
  in the delivered data.

## Consent

Consent is handled as a **separate datastream** from the questionnaires, so
that participation status can be managed independently of the substantive
responses.

- **Consent capture** — participants provide informed consent, recorded via
  Nettskjema.
- **Identification lookups** — consent processing maintains lookup tables that
  map a participant's Nettskjema `submission_reference`, phone number, or email
  to their `deltaker_id`.
- **Revocation** — participants may withdraw at any time. Withdrawn
  participants are recorded on a revoked-consent list, and their responses are
  removed during processing.

::: {.callout-important}
Consent is not a one-time gate. Revoked consents are re-applied on **every**
processing run, so a withdrawal removes the participant from all subsequently
delivered datasets. Analyses are always run against the current consent state.
:::

## From Nettskjema to TSD

Questionnaire and consent data move from Nettskjema into the secure environment
automatically:

1. Participants submit responses in Nettskjema.
2. The **TSD data loader** transfers submissions into TSD as raw,
   semicolon-delimited CSV files (one file per questionnaire form).
3. Inside TSD, each raw file is processed independently into a cleaned,
   labelled per-form dataset.

Because TSD has **no network access**, everything downstream of this transfer —
cleaning, linkage, analysis — happens entirely within TSD. No study data is
stored or processed outside it.

## Health registry linkage

For consenting participants, national health registries contribute records that
extend the self-reported data with objective, longitudinal health information.
Registry data is delivered to TSD as approved extracts and linked to
participants on the study key.

| Registry | Full name | Contributes |
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| **MSIS** | Meldingssystem for smittsomme sykdommer | Notifiable infectious-disease diagnoses (incl. SARS-CoV-2) |
| **SYSVAK** | Nasjonalt vaksinasjonsregister | Vaccinations (incl. COVID-19 doses) |
| **DÅR** | Dødsårsaksregisteret | Cause-of-death records |
| **NPR** | Norsk pasientregister | Hospital / specialist-care contacts |
| **LMR** | Legemiddelregisteret | Dispensed prescription medications |

::: {.callout-note}
Registry data is often **longitudinal** (multiple events per participant over
time). Before delivery it is summarised to one row per participant so it stays
joinable on `deltaker_id` without inflating row counts. What each registry
extract covers (time span, event types) is fixed by the approved data delivery.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Some registry deliveries carry strict handling conditions — for example, a
national identity number may be prohibited from being stored alongside the
registry records, with linkage performed through a project-specific key only.
These conditions are enforced in processing and are why registry data lives in
the most restricted storage tier.
:::

## Biological samples

The study also collects biological material and derived laboratory results.

- **Dried blood spots (DBS)** and related samples are collected from
  participants.
- Laboratory analyses (e.g. **serology** / antibody measurements) are performed
  and the results delivered to TSD.
- Biobank results are linked to participants on `deltaker_id` and processed the
  same way as other sources.

## Participant identification

Every source above is linked to a single key, `deltaker_id`, which is what
allows questionnaires, registries, and biobank data to be joined together.

During processing, `deltaker_id` is assigned by matching each response against
the consent lookup tables, in order of reliability:

1. Nettskjema `submission_reference`
2. Phone number
3. Email address

Once assigned, `deltaker_id` is the **only** identifier retained for linkage;
direct contact details (phone, email) are dropped from processed data. See
[Data management](../best-practices/data-management.qmd) for how `deltaker_id`
is used to join datasets.

All person-level data is stored and processed exclusively within **TSD**, under
tiered access controls that separate researcher-accessible data from the most
sensitive administrative data. Only aggregated results — never person-level
data — are brought out of TSD.
